scope: Independent design review of the bounded native ordinary-Claude partial-result round trip; not implementation or native acceptance.

scores.rationale: The proposed route uses existing ordinary selection, session, scoring, and result paths, with the live Guest/no-reminder baseline and category-specific stop/preservation checks. No new product semantics, data seeding, or runtime bridge is introduced.

criteria.evidence: The source-bound Claude feasibility probe shows a fresh ordinary 40-session is all single-choice, then an ordinary follow-on selection from its 40 production-created attempts includes six multiple-choice questions. The plan observes the actual device prepared question and does not replace or seed it.
criteria.limit: The in-memory probe does not predict the live account's exact selection; the device operator must stop if the prepared question is not partial-capable.

criteria.evidence: The real choice_multiple scorer returns partial for a complete one-of-two accepted selection. The accepted overallScoreCredit rule awards points only when result.kind is correct, so the partial contributes zero overall credit while its raw result kind/count remain available.
criteria.limit: This is source and accepted-contract evidence, not observation of native feedback or result display.

criteria.evidence: The read-only baseline records GCP goal revision 1 and accepted plan revision 4 linked to goal revision 1, with no active session or draft. Track selection stores the active track separately from track-specific goal/plan records. The plan compares prior GCP learning and plan categories after returning through the normal selector.
criteria.limit: The route changes the active track and creates intended Claude session/attempt records; only the live post-run category comparison can establish preservation on device.

criteria.evidence: The current baseline has no reminder settings/journal, zero scheduled notifications, and undetermined permission. Claude has no goal/plan. In this source branch, a missing Claude source is cleared without requesting permission; returning to GCP with no settings takes the existing disabled branch. Neither calls for reminder changes or scheduling.
criteria.limit: This conclusion applies only while the live pre-switch state matches the observed category values; the briefing requires a stop on unexpected source or selector state and post-run readback.

criteria.evidence: The baseline is Guest with no profile transition. A private follow-up found account-sign-out status pending and account-sync status failed, but no materialization, pending confirmation, reset guard, or sync plan. The brief now explicitly preserves these markers and forbids auth/profile transitions. Source tracing shows the pending mark does not rewrite a failed sync state, and scoped sign-out recovery is not entered by the ordinary no-auth Guest route.
criteria.limit: The root operator must stop if unexpected recovery UI or lifecycle effects appear; this review does not inspect account identifiers or authorize lifecycle recovery.

criteria.evidence: The operator uses existing selectors and session routes, observes actual immutable session/question IDs, completes both sessions, returns to GCP, reads named preservation categories, and does not retry uncertain effects blindly.

checks: Read the complete proposal and actual device preflight, including the updated lifecycle projection.
Traced active-track write order, account pending marking, guest/authenticated session branches, and reminder reconciliation branches.
Traced ordinary Focus Practice selection and canonical multiple-choice score/result-credit paths.
No device, account, reminder, app, source, or Git state was changed; no implementation test or native flow was run.
limitations: This review accepts only the proposed procedure, not its live native execution.
The runtime-selected follow-on question remains an observation; the plan correctly stops if it is not a supported multiple-choice item.
Post-run GCP plan/progress and lifecycle marker readback remain required for native acceptance.
No full Q12, full BIZQ-01, notification-delivery, whole-store-preservation, Premium, or release claim is made.
